config.title: justify-content

intro.title: justify-content
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple navigation bar to learn how to control the horizontal alignment of items within a flex container. You will use the CSS property `justify-content` to distribute space between and around navigation links. This core concept allows you to align flex items along the main axis, which is horizontal by default. The main technology involved is CSS Flexbox, specifically the `justify-content` property with values like `flex-start`, `center`, `space-between`, and `space-around`. By the end, you'll understand how to use `justify-content` to create clean, responsive layouts. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to one of the key properties in CSS Flexbox.
intro.usecase: The justify-content property is essential for creating responsive layouts in modern web interfaces. You'll use it to horizontally align navigation items in website headers, position form controls in centered login panels, and distribute dashboard widgets evenly across available space. This CSS property appears in product dashboards like analytics tools where cards need consistent spacing, e-commerce filter panels with aligned checkboxes, and social media feeds where content cards maintain uniform distribution. Mastering justify-content helps you build professional interfaces that adapt cleanly to different screen sizes and content amounts.

objectives: Apply the justify-content property to a flex container.
Configure flex items to align along the main axis using values like flex-start and flex-end.
Manipulate spacing between flex items using space-between and space-around.
Construct a layout that centers content horizontally within a flex container.
Update existing CSS to change the justification of flex items dynamically.
Integrate justify-content with other flexbox properties to control overall layout.

steps.title: Create a container element with display: flex
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a class named 'container' that sets display to flex. This will make it a flex container where justify-content can be applied.
steps.hint: Use the class selector .container followed by curly braces, then add the display property with the value flex inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule for .container with display: flex is created, establishing a flex container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've set display to flex inside the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .container rule should have display: flex to create a flex container. Try again.

steps.title: Add child elements to the flex container
steps.instruction: Create three child elements inside the flex container by adding CSS rules for .item1, .item2, and .item3 classes. Give each a width of 80px, height of 80px, and different background colors.
steps.hint: Add three CSS rules targeting .item1, .item2, and .item3. Set width, height, and background-color properties for each.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three child elements with distinct colors will be ready inside the flex container for justify-content distribution.
successCriteria: CSS rules for .item1, .item2, and .item3 are created, each with width: 80px, height: 80px, and unique background colors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created some child elements, but make sure you have all three (.item1, .item2, .item3) with width: 80px, height: 80px, and distinct background colors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The child elements aren't properly defined. Create three CSS rules for .item1, .item2, and .item3, each with width: 80px, height: 80px, and different background colors.

steps.title: Apply justify-content: flex-start to the container
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property justify-content: flex-start to the .container rule.
steps.hint: Inside the .container selector, add a new line with justify-content: flex-start;
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have justify-content: flex-start applied, aligning items to the start of the container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added justify-content: flex-start; inside the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add justify-content: flex-start; to the .container selector to align items to the start.

steps.title: Change justify-content to flex-end
steps.instruction: In the .container rule, change the justify-content value from flex-start to flex-end.
steps.hint: Update the CSS property value to align items to the end of the flex container.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will align to the end of the container (right side in LTR layout).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you changed the justify-content value to flex-end in the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The justify-content value in the .container rule should be flex-end, not flex-start.

steps.title: Apply justify-content: center
steps.instruction: Change the container's justify-content value from flex-start to center.
steps.hint: Update the justify-content property in the .container selector to use the value 'center'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will be centered along the main axis (horizontally by default) within the container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've updated the justify-content property in the .container selector to 'center'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The justify-content value should be changed to 'center' in the .container selector.

steps.title: Add visual styling to see the justify-content effects clearly
steps.instruction: Add background colors, padding, and margins to the .container and .item elements to enhance visibility of the justify-content behavior.
steps.hint: Use background-color, padding, and margin properties. For example, give the container a light background and items distinct colors.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container and items will have visible background colors and spacing, making the justify-content alignment more apparent.
successCriteria: The .container has background-color, padding, and/or margin. Each .item1, .item2, .item3 has background-color, padding, and/or margin.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some styling, but ensure both the container and all items have background colors and spacing.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding background-color, padding, and margin to the container and each item.

steps.title: Create a second container with different justify-c
steps.instruction: Create a second CSS class named .container2 with display: flex and a different justify-content value (choose any value you've learned).
steps.hint: Define a new CSS rule starting with .container2 {}. Inside, set display: flex and justify-content to a value like flex-start, center, space-around, etc. Then create three .item2 rules with basic styling.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have two distinct flex containers: .container with space-between and .container2 with your chosen justify-content value, each with their own child elements.
successCriteria: A .container2 class is defined with display: flex and a justify-content value different from space-between. Three .item2 rules are created with basic styling properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure .container2 has both display: flex and a justify-content value, and that you've created three .item2 rules with styling.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't yet include a .container2 class with flex display and a different justify-content value, or the required .item2 child elements. Review the instruction and try again.
